dedupe_keys.name: fmi recordings of geomagnetically induced currents gic in the finnish natural gas pipeline at mantsala 10 second data with numeric files

description: The Finnish Meteorological Institute publishes recordings of geomagnetically induced currents in the Finnish natural gas pipeline network, measured close to the Mantsala compressor station in southern Finland at 60.6 degrees north, 25.2 degrees east. Each daily plot shows the current in the pipeline as 10-second values (1-minute averages before 27 February 2023), with eastward current positive, above the time derivative of the geomagnetic north component at the Nurmijarvi Observatory about 40 kilometres to the west, which follows the east geoelectric field closely. The pages offer final data, preliminary quick-look data and a near-real-time view, and state that numeric data files are available; recording stopped on 23 October 2023. FMI has worked with Fingrid and Gasum since the 1970s on GIC in the power and gas networks, and cites a 2001 paper on the recordings. Access: free to view on the FMI space weather server; the final data carry only a cursory quality check with noise and error spikes, and the preliminary data ask users to contact FMI before presenting them; no licence is stated. Coverage is one pipeline site. Caveats: the numeric file format was not visible, and the series ended in 2023. It suits hazard exposure and resilience studies of pipelines under space weather, and relates to the May 2024 storm GIC observations record catalogued here.
